DILG BACONC Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City DILG OPINION No. FRISCO T. VILLA 309 Purok 4, Poblacion West, Pantabangan, Nueva Ecija Villafrisc052@gmaiI.com Dear Mr. Villa: This has reference to to your letter dated 19 April 2024, in relation to your letter to Mayor Roberto T. Agdipa dated 24 January 2024, and the latter's response to said letter dated 02 April 2024, stating that the documents / information being requested in your letter appears to be violative of Republic Act No. 10173, also known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012 ("DPA"), as amended, and does not conform with the substance required of said law. Under this premise arose the request for guidance on whether the following would violate the provisions of the DPA: 1. List of names of Job Order employees and their respective salaries mentioned in the COA Audit Report for Pantabangan, Nueva Ecija for the year ending in 2017; 2. List of consultants of the municipal government of Pantabangan, and their salaries, from July 2016 to date; 3. Abstract / list of bidders and the contract between the winning bidder and the Pantabangan government relative to the rehabilitation of the water system in Pantabangan; 4. Action taken by the municipal government or update on the P55 million unliquidated cash advances of officials and employees of Pantabangan as per COA audit reports for the years ending in 2017, 2018 and the years thereafter At the onset, considering that the ISt and 2nd items are interrelated, we deem it proper to tackle the same in one discussion. Accordingly, we would like to emphasize that Section 4 of the Data Privacy Act of 2012, as amended, explicitly provides that its provisions are not applicable in the following cases: a) Information about anv individual who is or was an officer or employee of a qovernment institution that relates to the position or functions of the individual, including: "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

1) The fact that the individual is or was an officer or employee of the government institution; 2) The title, business address and office telephone number of the individual; 3) The classification. salary. range and responsibilities of the position held by the individual; and 4) The name of the individual on a document prepared by the individual in the course of employment with the government; b) Information about an individual who is or was performing service under contract for a qovernment institution that relates to the services performed, including the terms of the contract, and the name of the individual given in the course of the performance of those services; c) Information relatinq to anv discretionary benefit of a financial nature such as the grantinq of a license or permit qiven bv the government to an individual. includinq the name of the individual and the exact nature Of the benefit, d) xxx xxx xxx [Emphasis and underscoring supplied.] Moreover, as previously emphasized in DILG Opinion No. 63 S. 2019, Section 5(e) of Republic Act No. 6713 (R.A. 6713), provide that all public documents must be made accessible to, and readily available for inspection by, the public within reasonable hours. Correspondingly, Section 3 of the Implementing Rules and Regulation of R.A. 6713 provides that every department, office or agency shall provide official information, records or documents to any requesting public, subject to certain exceptions. In addition, DILG Opinion No. 63 S. 2019, which states that "barangay payroll is regarded as official record/document in the custody of a government agency/official which must be accessible to the public", is also applicable to the payroll of the city local government unit. Hence, the information being requested under the ISt and 2nd items would not violate the provisions of the DPA. As to the 3rd and 4th items, while we recognize that certain documents related to procurement are made public by the procuring entity, however, we are of the position that the disclosure may be assessed by the procuring entity on a case-to-case basis, taking into account the general data privacy principles. Specifically, the following considerations: purpose of the request must be legitimate and not contrary to law, morals, or public policy, and the personal data requested must be necessary to the declared, specified, and legitimate purpose; document requested is not excessive in relation to the declared and specified purpose of the request; redaction of personal data, where appropriate, should also be considered; and determine whether abstracts, statistics, or aggregated data will suffice for the purpose of the request. Lastly, on the action taken by the municipal government or update on the P55 million unliquidated cash advances of officials and employees of Pantabangan as per COA audit reports for the years ending in 2017, 2018 and the years thereafter, we bring to your attention this Department's Memorandum Circular No. 2024-0211, relative to Full I Entitled: REVISED IMPLEMENTING GUIDELINES ON THE FULL DISCLOSURE POLICY (FDP) AND Page 2 of 3

Disclosure Policy (FDP), the purpose of which is to sustain the transparent practices of LGUs. Under the FDP, LGUs are to fully disclose particular financial documents in at least three (3) conspicuous places and in the FDP Portal, to keep their constituents informed on how the LGU budget is managed, disbursed and used. It primarily aims to promote honest, transparent, and Oderly management of public funds, help minimize, if not totally prevent, corruption and misuse of public funds and increase the awareness on the available public funds and the allocated amount for development projects in their localities. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you.
